name: Muslim Brotherhood
summary: The Muslim Brotherhood's founding ideology, set out by Hasan al-Banna in 1928-49, holds Islam to be a comprehensive system of creed, state, law, economy and morals, with the Qur'an as the constitution. It seeks to rebuild the individual, the Islamic home and then society before an Islamic government, to free Muslim lands from foreign control and restore Muslim unity under a caliphate, and to enforce Islamic morals through law, schooling and censorship while pressing for social justice, zakat and an end to usury. It treats jihad as an obligation, rejects the separation of religion and state, and distrusts party rivalry yet works within existing institutions and gradual reform.

scope: The Muslim Brotherhood as a set of ideas: the programme Hasan al-Banna set out in the Society of the Muslim Brothers from 1928 until his death in 1949 (Toward the Light, The Message of the Teachings and his Fifth Conference message), as described by scholars and reference works. Where Banna-era texts are silent or later Brotherhood statements and party platforms differ (women's political rights, party politics, the 1994 and 2007 documents), the profile answers null or records a split, and it does not use them. It excludes national branches (Jordan, Syria, Sudan, Libya), the Brotherhood's governments and the thought of Sayyid Qutb, which belongs to qutbism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and the Armed Forces' calls military strength a stringent duty and puts it among a renascent nation's needs.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) asks for laws protecting the family and encouraging marriage.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Message of the Teachings tells the Brother to be tender, mild and gentle towards people and animals.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 4) calls for liberating the homeland from foreign control and (jihad principle) makes fighting the highest degree of jihad, and Johnston and Mura record the Brotherhood's 1947-48 Palestine campaign.

arms-reduction.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and Public Health' says a renascent nation needs a superior military force.

ban-interest.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (economic) calls for prohibiting usury and organising banks accordingly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) has theatres, films, songs and broadcasts watched and censored for morality, and provocative stories, books and newspapers confiscated.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and the Armed Forces' quotes the Prophet's counsel to commanders not to kill women, children and the aged and presents it as the mark of Islam's military force.

civilizational-union.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (political) asks for closer bonds among Islamic countries to pave the way for the departed caliphate, and The Message of the Teachings (steps 6 and 7) aims at the Umma's unity and the restored Khilafah.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 4) demands liberation from foreign control of every kind, and Euben and Zaman describe Banna's work against foreign domination.

clerical-rule.rationale: Toward the Light, 'The Clerics Are Not Religion Itself' says the religious authorities' jurisdiction in Islam is limited and that every Muslim is a religious authority.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 4) calls for liberating the homeland from foreign political and economic control, and Euben and Zaman present Banna as moved by natives working for foreign profit.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 5) calls the Islamic government a servant of the nation that the people may dismiss, and Fondren's section on ideology reports Banna's social-contract picture of a ruler contracted by the people, though he calls that picture tenuous.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Toward the Light, 'A Bold Step but a Successful One' says Europe's pursuit of luxuries and coveted possessions convulsed it and destroys nations, and the economic steps put necessary projects before luxuries.

culture-before-state.rationale: In The Message of the Teachings the individual, home and society come before the Islamic government (step 5), and El-Ghobashy notes that for Banna Islamising society, not winning a state, came first.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Western Civilization Today' calls the West bankrupt and in decline, and 'Islam and Morality' says Islam alone can create a perfect soul.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (the principle on jihad) calls jihad a divinely ordained obligation whose highest degree is fighting in God's way, and Toward the Light, 'Islam and the Armed Forces' quotes Q 4:75 on fighting for the oppressed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 4) calls for liberation from all foreign control, political, economic or ideological.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (political) asks for an end to party rivalry, and Johnston says Banna condemned the multiparty system.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) wants girls' curricula distinct from boys', segregation of the sexes and women's reform that is protective as well as progressive, and Freer notes his separate women's division.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Mura's account of Banna's 1930s pamphlets reports the aim of establishing Allah's sovereignty and calls for the sovereignty of God in every section of society, and The Message of the Teachings ties the duty to obey rulers to God ('No obedience is due to a creature in disobedience to the Creator').

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and National Greatness' quotes Q 3:110 ('the best nation') for the Muslim community.

dominated-front.rationale: Mura reports Banna's picture of the East as one battalion ready to meet the ranks of the West.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) targets harmful customs and ostentation in dress and asks for a gradual uniform mode of dress.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 5) lets non-Muslims be employed only if they are not given positions of leadership, and Toward the Light, 'Islam Protects Minorities and Safeguards the Rights of Foreigners' offers benevolence and justice to non-Muslims but bars those it counts as enemies.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Mura shows Banna rejecting nationalism built on race and ethnicity and defining the community by the Islamic creed.

gradual-change.rationale: The Message of the Teachings lays out stages (introduction, formation, execution) and seven successive steps from the individual upward, and Euben and Zaman and Mura both describe his strategy as gradual change from the ground up.

harm-principle.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) has the state punish private moral offences, ban gambling and drink, and treat private meetings of men and women as a crime.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (education) wants Islamic history, national history and national culture cultivated in schooling.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Mura shows Banna defining patriotism through the Islamic creed, including affection for the homeland, freedom and greatness.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 4) calls for liberation from foreign control, political, economic and ideological, and Toward the Light (economic steps) moves foreign-held projects into the national sector.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Toward the Light, 'The Fundamental Sources of the Renaissance in the East Are Not Those of the West' rejects separating religion from the state and says what happened in Europe is inappropriate for conditions in the East.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Toward the Light has 'The Fundamental Sources of the Renaissance in the East Are Not Those of the West' and 'Western Civilization Today' against borrowing the West's foundations, but also 'Islam Is Not a Disturbing Influence on Relations with the West', and Johnston reports the Brotherhood's readiness to use Western ideas and technology.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Hoffmann reports that by 1948 Banna openly voiced anti-Zionist views, and Mura records the Brotherhood's military contribution to the 1948 war.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (political) demands that legislation conform to Islamic legislation in every branch, and The Message of the Teachings makes 'The Qur'an is our constitution' a slogan and names the Qur'an and Sunnah as the references. The Oxford dictionary entry also states the aim of an Islamic state under the Qur'an.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) calls for a campaign against drugs and for prohibition of drink.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) demands an end to prostitution.

limit-population.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) seeks to encourage marriage and procreation by every means.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and the Armed Forces' honours those who give their lives in God's way as sacrificing something of great value.

military-superiority.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and the Armed Forces' calls military strength a stringent duty and 'Islam and Public Health' says a renascent nation needs a superior military force.

morality-needs-religion.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and Morality' says only Islam can create the perfect soul and that no organised body of law reaches the heart as religion does.

more-religion-public.rationale: In Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' puts law, schooling, government service, the press and entertainment under Islamic rule, and The Message of the Teachings opens by calling Islam a comprehensive system covering state, nation, law and jihad. Britannica describes the society as religiopolitical and urging a return to the Qur'an and Hadith.

national-rebirth.rationale: Johnston's entry says the Brotherhood sought a complete spiritual revival (nahda) of society, and Toward the Light ('At the Crossroads', 'Islam and National Greatness') calls for renewal after the West's decline.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Message of the Teachings makes jihad up to fighting an obligation, and Toward the Light, 'Islam and the Armed Forces' calls military strength a duty.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (education) wants religious instruction in all schools and Qur'an memorisation.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (economic) wants zakat organised to aid the aged, the poor and orphans.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (political) requires law to conform to Islamic legislation, and Mura says shari'a inspires legislation in Banna's Islamised state rather than Parliament standing above it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) has broadcasts watched and censored and offending newspapers confiscated, which puts the news media under state control.

patriotic-education.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (education) wants the first school stage to instil a virtuous, patriotic spirit.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (political) and The Message of the Teachings (step 6) both look to closer bonds among Islamic countries leading to the restored caliphate.

premarital-sex.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) calls fornication a detestable crime whose perpetrator must be flogged.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (education and the home) wants Islamic and national history and culture cultivated and the foreign spirit in homes replaced by an Egyptian one.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Message of the Teachings makes the Qur'an the constitution and has government enforce Islamic law, and Fondren (section on ideology) reports that Banna held the ruler bound by Islam's teachings.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) asks for encouragement of marriage and procreation by all possible means.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) asks for punishment of insulting the faith, alongside penalties for breaking the Ramadan fast and neglecting prayer.

racial-pride.rationale: Mura reports Banna calling racial self-aggrandizement that disparages other races incompatible with Islam.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (economic) asks for protecting the masses from monopolistic companies and keeping them within strict limits.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Message of the Teachings says an Imam's opinion on public benefit may change with circumstances and that uncertain Islamic principles should be reinterpreted where they seem to contradict established science.

religious-nation.rationale: Mura shows Banna defining the 'Islamic homeland' by Islamic brotherhood, in contrast to bonds of 'geographic', 'ethnic' or 'racial' factors such as 'nationalism' and 'patriotism', so the nation is the community of the faith.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: In The Message of the Teachings (step 5, the Islamic government) a government that neglects its duties is to be advised, then dismissed and removed by the people, since the Qur'an is the constitution.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The Message of the Teachings counts speaking a word of truth to a tyrannical ruler within jihad, and addresses Brothers resolved to live by their call and die on its path.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) censors films and songs and confiscates provocative stories and books, with no exemption for private adult use.

sacred-nation.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Islam and National Greatness' says the nation's nobility and honour have been sanctified by God, and quotes Q 3:110 on the best nation.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (principles on the Qur'an) says the whole of the Qur'an is from our Lord and counts denial of its purity as unbelief.

separate-church-state.rationale: Toward the Light, 'The Fundamental Sources of the Renaissance in the East Are Not Those of the West' rejects definitively separating religion from the general policy of the state.

separated-powers.rationale: Mura reports that Banna accepted liberal tools in principle, naming the separation of powers and Parliament.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 2) puts the Islamic home's household under the head's supervision.

simple-living.rationale: Toward the Light, 'A Bold Step but a Successful One' warns against the luxuries and comforts that wrecked Europe, and the economic steps give necessary projects priority over luxury.

single-common-good.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (political) asks for an end to party rivalry and a single common front.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 5) has the people dismiss a government that neglects its duties, and Fondren (section on ideology) reports that the ruler must be bound by the teachings of Islam.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Johnston says the Brotherhood aimed at a complete spiritual revival of society, together with social welfare and an Islamic state.

state-harmful.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 5) lists duties of the Islamic government, and Johnston reports the society's core belief that there can be no Islamic society without an Islamic state.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (education) puts religious instruction in every school, the opposite of state-promoted atheism.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: Toward the Light, 'Some Steps toward Practical Reform' (social) has the state penalise moral offences, censor entertainment, close dance halls, and encourage marriage and family.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Johnston describes the Brotherhood's pragmatism that sanctions Western ideas and technology as tools for advancing Islam.

traditional-family.rationale: The Message of the Teachings (step 2) makes establishing an Islamic home, with the household under the head's supervision, the second stage of reform, and Toward the Light (social steps) wants marriage encouraged and legislation protecting the family.

universal-morality.rationale: Toward the Light ('Islam and Morality') and The Message of the Teachings (step 7, guiding the world) present Islam's moral teaching as meant for all humanity.

notes: Scope departure: the record the driver supplied marked this entry as an organisation (notIdeasOfWhatSocietyShouldBe). PROMPT.md's first check asks only whether two statements can be answered from stated positions, and the Brotherhood's founding texts answer more than seventy, so this profile treats it as a set of ideas and removes that record. Answers rest on Banna's own texts (s7, s8) and on scholarship describing them; statements those texts do not touch stay null. Questions on which Banna-era texts and later Brotherhood documents differ were not settled from the later documents: women's suffrage and office, parties and elections (Banna condemned parties yet ran in 1942 and 1945), apostasy, and the elective head of state (Fondren hedges that point). Names left out of the aliases though Wikipedia redirects them here: Ikhwanweb (the society's website), Libyan Muslim Brotherhood (a branch), Islam is the solution (a slogan), Party of the Muslim Brotherhood (a party), and generic forms such as Islamic brotherhood and Al-Ikhwan. s6 and s7 are one saved file: the Euben and Zaman chapter, whose editors' introduction is scholarly s6 and whose translation of Toward the Light is primary s7. Wikipedia (s1) was read through scripts/wiki.js for orientation and is cited by no answer. The Al Jazeera Arabic article (Shuqayr, 2004) was dropped: the validator cannot match Arabic-script names, so it counts as never naming the ideology, and no Arabic alias passes the everyday-word check (source number s10 is left unused). Saved but not used: the Carnegie draft party platform (a later platform), the Our Message PDF (garbled two-column text), an e-ir.info essay (landing page only), areq.net and drzedan.com (copies of the Twenty Principles that s8 already covers), and Lia's article on Banna's memoirs (opened, not cited). Of the 21 downloaded books only Fondren (s3) and Hoffmann (s11) were read and used. Of the Arabic books only three (the two by Ali and the one by Said) were searched, and only for women's political rights, where the hits describe 1990s-2000s statements outside this scope; the others (Jayyar, Ashraf, Atiyah, Ghanim, Shammakh, Thubaytat) were not opened for answers; the DTIC reports and Leckie's thesis were searched only for Banna (they assess the movement rather than state its tenets), and the Sudan, America, Syria, Jordan, Idwi, Hameed Ud Din and Israel State Archives items are about other subjects or branches and were not used.
